intro: Section 32.1 follows normal development from conception to the end of adolescence: prenatal brain development and the effects of maternal stress, genetic disorders and drugs (including fetal alcohol syndrome); infant reflexes, motor, language and cognitive milestones and Piaget's stages; emotional development, temperament, attachment (Harlow, Bowlby, Ainsworth) and Mahler's separation-individuation; the toddler, preschool and school-age years, with play, sibling rivalry, school refusal, birth order, divorce and parenting styles; and adolescence, with its stages, physical and sexual maturation, cognitive and moral development, sexual behavior, risk-taking, substance use, violence and exploitation. US figures and laws are as the book gives them. Update boxes add the 2022 CDC and AAP milestone checklists and screening ages, the DSM-5 attachment disorders, ND-PAE and alcohol in pregnancy, recent US teen birth and drug-use data, the Dobbs decision, and Philippine laws on newborn screening, early childhood care, age of sexual consent, bullying and trafficking.
objectives: Describe prenatal nervous system development and the main prenatal risks, including the features of fetal alcohol syndrome.
Recognize normal motor, language, cognitive and social milestones from infancy to school age, and Piaget's stages.
Compare temperament dimensions, attachment types in the Strange Situation and Mahler's subphases, and explain how deprivation affects development.
Explain how family factors such as birth order, divorce, step-families, daycare and parenting style shape development.
Distinguish normal adolescent turmoil from psychopathology and describe the stages and components of adolescence, including sexual maturity ratings.
Identify adolescent risk behaviors (sexual activity, substance use, violence, bullying, sexual offending and exploitation) and the clinician's role.
